body:
incident-bot: ALERT: High KV cache churn detected on prod-pool-1. error_rate + tail_latency rising. paging oncall team. link: https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/1769581234 :rotating_light:
ryan-oncall: Ack. I'm online. Pulling metrics now.
maya: I'm joining, looking at prefix cache heatmap and tokenizer churn.
sam-eng: tagging in — saw a blip in batching RTs earlier, could be continuous-batching growing keyspace.
lena: customers showing increased 5xx on hosted API, some clients experiencing ~3x latency. CS flagged a high-traffic customer.
maya: quick snapshot from `kv-metrics`:

```
kv_keys_total{pool="prod-pool-1"} 1.8e7
kv_keys_active{pool="prod-pool-1"} 1.7e7
kv_ttl_evictions_per_min  0.2
batch_size_avg  24
inflight_requests  2300
```
maya: key cardinality jump at 09:12 UTC coincides with a model rollout (version 2.3.1) that updated prompt templates + tokenizer tweak. suspect prefix hashing mismatch + template drift.
ryan-oncall: can we confirm tokenizer version drift? which model was rolled?
maya: model `redwood-alpha-2.3.1` rolled at 09:10 UTC via canary -> global. The new prompt template added dynamic user metadata into prefix: `user.bio` expansion. That creates near-unique prefixes.
sam-eng: Oof. So deterministic template change caused near-unique prefixes -> KV cache blown up. Continuous batching is keeping KV entries hot longer. Need mitigation: stop unique prefix generation and throttle batching.
lena: customer-ops: Impacted customers: list shared in DM. Need ETA for mitigation and comms.
ryan-oncall: Immediate plan:
1) Disable continuous batching on prod-pool-1 to reduce KV retention.
2) Patch prompt template in rollout to revert dynamic `user.bio` expansion.
3) Increase KV eviction aggressiveness (shorten TTL) for current keys.
4) Page infra if eviction doesn't shrink mem within 5 mins.
I'll execute 1 and 3 now.
maya: I'll prepare the template rollback PR and a hotfix to strip user-specific fields from prefix keys.
sam-eng: Commands to run (running as ryan):
```
# disable continuous batching for pool
redwoodctl pools update prod-pool-1 --set continuous_batching=false
# tighten KV TTL
redwoodctl kv config set prod-pool-1 --prefixttl 60s
```
ryan-oncall: executed `redwoodctl pools update` -> response: `OK continuous_batching=false`
deploy-bot: deploy started: config-change/disable-batching by ryan-oncall at 09:18 UTC. CI checks passed.
ryan-oncall: executed `redwoodctl kv config set` -> response: `OK prefixTTL=60s`
maya: PR #4829 created to revert template: remove `user.bio` from prefix interpolation and sanitize dynamic fields. Link: https://git.internal/repo/pr/4829
sam-eng: Observability after changes (09:22 UTC snapshot):
```
kv_keys_active{pool="prod-pool-1"} 3.2e6  # down from 1.7e7
batch_size_avg  8
tail_p95_latency_ms  +70 -> +25
```
lena: nice. Customer-ops: triage message drafted for impacted customers: short blurb + mitigation steps + ETA for full fix. Want review?
customer-ops: shared draft: "We've identified a recent model template change that increased cache key cardinality causing higher latency. We've applied immediate mitigations and are rolling a template rollback. We'll follow up when stable." Thoughts?
ryan-oncall: fine. Add note: we removed user-specific fields from prefixes and tightened cache TTL. asking for SLO impact metrics in follow-up. :thumbsup: 
maya: rolling the template hotfix to prod canary now, will monitor key cardinality.
deploy-bot: deploy completed: pr-4829 -> canary at 09:28 UTC.
maya: canary looks good, key churn falling. scheduling global rollout in 5 mins.
sam-eng: also adding a safeguard: enforce prefix key normalization in runtime to strip high-entropy tokens. quick patch:
```
// pseudo
prefix = sanitize(prefix);
if (entropy(prefix) > 0.7) prefix = hash(prefix).slice(0,8);
```
I'll open PR for that.
ryan-oncall: global rollout started for pr-4829 at 09:34 UTC.
maya: global rollout success by 09:36 UTC. mem usage trending down.
lena: customer-ops: sending update to customers now with link to status page.
customer-ops: sent. response: one customer acknowledged, others queued.
ryan-oncall: monitoring for 30 mins. If stable, will close incident. Anyone want to add postmortem owners?
maya: I'll own the PM write-up for template drift and fix plan. Sam will own runtime hardening follow-up.
sam-eng: will add test coverage for prefix entropy and add a guardrail in the model rollout checklist to require prefix review.
deploy-bot: auto-notes: change set: disable-batching, kv-ttl-change, pr-4829 rollback.
ryan-oncall: Thanks team. Marking as mitigated. Will leave thread open for any late signals. :coffee:
maya: Recording next steps: 1) postmortem 24h, 2) add pre-rollout lint for prefix templates, 3) runtime sanitize PR, 4) add metric alert for rapid key cardinality increase (>2x in 5m).
customer-ops: also requesting a scheduled follow-up with top impacted customer to review mitigations.
ryan-oncall: closing in 30m if no regressions. Good job.
